title.raw: 卷十七 梁書17: 列傳七 成汭 杜洪 田頵 趙匡凝 張佶 雷滿 Volume 17 Book of Later Liang 17: Biographies 7 - Cheng Rui, Du Hong, Tian Yun, Zhao Kuangning, Zhang Ji, Lei Man

sentences.zh: 成汭，淮西人。

translations.literal: Cheng Rui was a native of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Rui came from west of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 少年任俠，乘醉殺人，為仇家所捕，因落發為僧，冒姓郭氏。

translations.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and bold, killed a man while drunk, was seized by the enemy family, and therefore shaved his head to become a monk and usurped the surname Guo.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he killed someone in a drunken brawl, was hunted by the victim's kin, shaved his head as a monk, and took the surname Guo.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Cheng Rui's alias:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Cheng Rui's alias:

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》云：入蔡賊中，為賊帥假子，更姓名為郭禹。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: entering Cai rebel bands, he became a rebel chief's adoptive son and changed his name to Guo Yu.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says he joined the Cai rebels as an adopted son and renamed himself Guo Yu.)〉

sentences.zh: 亡匿久之，及貴，方復本姓。

translations.literal: He hid in flight a long time; when he reached eminence he then restored his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in hiding for years and only restored his true name once he had risen.

sentences.zh: 唐僖宗朝，為蔡州軍校，領本郡兵戍荊南，帥以其凶暴，欲害之，遂棄本軍奔於秭歸。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xizong's Tang he was a Cai prefecture army officer, led the prefecture's troops to garrison Jingnan; the commander because of his ferocity wished to harm him, so he abandoned his army and fled to Zigui.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xizong he was a Caizhou officer garrisoning Jingnan until his commander, fearing his violence, tried to kill him; he fled to Zigui with his troops.

sentences.zh: 一夕，巨蛇繞其身，幾至於殞，乃祝曰：「苟有所負，死生惟命。

translations.literal: One night a huge serpent coiled around his body, almost to his death; he then prayed, saying: "If I bear some guilt, life and death are fate's alone.
translations.idiomatic: One night a giant snake coiled around him until he nearly died; he prayed, "If I am guilty, let fate decide.

sentences.zh: 」 逡巡，蛇亦解去。

translations.literal: " After a moment the serpent too unwound and left.
translations.idiomatic: " In time the snake loosened and slid away.

sentences.zh: 後據歸州，招集流亡，練士伍，得兵千餘人，沿流以襲荊南，遂據其地。

translations.literal: Later he seized Guizhou, gathered fugitives, drilled soldiers, obtained more than a thousand troops, along the river struck Jingnan, and thus held that territory.
translations.idiomatic: He took Guizhou, rallied refugees into a thousand-man force, sailed downriver against Jingnan, and seized it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷即以旄鉞授之。

translations.literal: The court at once granted him command pennant and axe.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon invested him with full military command.

sentences.zh: 是時荊州經巨盜之後，居民才一十七家，汭撫輯凋殘，勵精為理，通商訓農，勤於惠養，比及末年，僅及萬戶。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhou after great bandits had only seventeen resident households; Rui pacified the devastated ruin, strove in governance, opened commerce and trained farming, diligently in nurturing kindness—by his last years barely reaching ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou after the great devastations held only seventeen households; Rui rebuilt trade and agriculture until, by his last years, the city neared ten thousand families.

sentences.zh: 汭性豪暴，事皆意斷，又好自矜伐，騁辯淩人，深為識者所鄙。

translations.literal: Rui's nature was arrogant and violent; affairs were all decided by his own intent; he also loved self-praise, vaunted eloquence to overbear others, and was deeply despised by the knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was domineering, arrogant in debate, and widely scorned by men of judgment.

sentences.zh: 初，澧、朗二州，本屬荊南，乾寧中，為土豪雷滿所據。

translations.literal: At first Li and Lang two prefectures originally belonged to Jingnan; in Qianning they were held by local strongman Lei Man.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Lang, once part of Jingnan, fell to the local strongman Lei Man in Qianning.

sentences.zh: 汭奏請割隸，唐宰相徐彥若執而不行，汭由是銜之。

translations.literal: Rui memorialized requesting to detach and subordinate them; Tang chancellor Xu Yanruo held firm and did not carry it out; Rui thereby harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Rui asked the court to annex them; Chancellor Xu Yanruo refused, and Rui nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及彥若出鎮南海，路過江陵，汭雖加延接，而猶怏怏。

translations.literal: When Yanruo went out to command Nanhai, passing Jiangling, Rui though adding courtesies was still displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanruo passed Jiangling en route to his Nanhai post, Rui received him coldly despite the courtesies.

sentences.zh: 嘗因對酒，語及其事，彥若曰：「令公位尊方面，自比桓、文。

translations.literal: Once over wine he spoke of the matter; Yanruo said: "My lord's position is honored in your quarter, comparing yourself to Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At wine Yanruo said, "You rank yourself with Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 雷滿者，偏州一草賊爾，令公盍不加兵，而反怨朝廷乎！

translations.literal: Lei Man is but a petty prefecture grass bandit—why does my lord not send troops instead of resenting the court!"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet you resent the court over Lei Man, a mere frontier bandit—why not march against him instead?"

sentences.zh: 」汭赧然而屈。

translations.literal: " Rui blushed and was subdued.
translations.idiomatic: " Rui flushed and fell silent.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on lacuna in the text:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on lacuna in the text:

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The text below is lost.)〉

sentences.zh: 累官至檢校太尉，封上穀郡王。

translations.literal: In succession he reached honorary Grand General and was enfeoffed Prince of Shanggu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to honorary Grand General and was made Prince of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 楊行密以兵圍鄂州，汭出師以援鄂，淮寇乘之，以火焚其艦，汭投江而死。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi with troops besieged Ezhou; Rui marched out to relieve E; Huainan raiders seized the moment, used fire to burn his warships; Rui threw himself in the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmi besieged Ezhou, Rui sailed to relieve it; the Huainan fleet burned his ships and he drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖以汭歿於王事，上表於唐帝，請為汭立廟於荊門，優詔可之。

translations.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder because Rui died in royal service memorialized the Tang emperor requesting a temple for Rui at Jingmen; gracious edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder had the Tang court approve a temple for Rui at Jingmen, honoring his death in service.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Zheng Zhun from the 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Zheng Zhun from the 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》:

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：鄭準，不知何許人，性諒直，能為文章，長於箋奏。

translations.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Zheng Zhun, origin unknown, nature frank and upright, able at writing, skilled at memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplement》 says Zheng Zhun, of unknown origin, was upright, literate, and expert at memorials.

sentences.zh: 成汭鎮荊南，辟為推官。

translations.literal: Cheng Rui garrisoned Jingnan and recruited him as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Rui held Jingnan he made Zhun his investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 汭嘗仇殺人，懼為吏所捕，改姓郭氏。

translations.literal: Rui once killed in feud; fearing capture by officers, changed surname to Guo.
translations.idiomatic: After a feud killing he had taken the surname Guo to evade the law.

sentences.zh: 及為荊南節度使，命準為表，乞歸本姓。

translations.literal: When he became Jingnan military commissioner, ordered Zhun to draft a memorial begging restoration of original surname.
translations.idiomatic: As Jingnan commissioner he had Zhun draft a memorial to restore the name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 準援筆而成，其略云：「臣門非冠蓋，家本軍戎。

translations.literal: Zhun took brush and completed it; gist said: "Your subject's house is not of noble caps and canopies; family origin is military camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun wrote at once; it began, "My house wears no court caps; my family comes from the army.

sentences.zh: 親朋之內，盱睢為人報怨；

translations.literal: Among kin and friends, glaring and gnashing to avenge others;
translations.idiomatic: Among kin and friends, eyes glaring to settle others' scores;

sentences.zh: 昆弟之間，點染無處求生。

translations.literal: Among brothers, stained with nowhere to seek life.
translations.idiomatic: Among brothers, marked with blood and nowhere to live.

sentences.zh: 背故國以狐疑，望鄰封而鼠竄。

translations.literal: Turning back on the old state in hesitant doubt, looking to neighboring borders and fleeing like a rat.
translations.idiomatic: I turned from my homeland in doubt and scurried to a neighbor like a cornered rat.

sentences.zh: 名非霸越，乘舟難效於陶朱；

translations.literal: Name not Ba and Yue, boarding a boat hard to emulate Tao Zhu;
translations.idiomatic: I was no lord of Wu or Yue—by boat I could not follow Fan Li;

sentences.zh: 誌切投秦，出境遂稱於張祿。

translations.literal: Aspiration keen to throw in with Qin, crossing the border then styled as Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: My heart set on Qin, I crossed the border and called myself Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「成為本姓，郭乃冒稱。

translations.literal: " Also said: "Cheng is the original surname; Guo is usurped claim.
translations.idiomatic: " It added, "Cheng is my true name; Guo was a borrowed lie.

sentences.zh: 本避犯禁之辜，敢歸司寇；

translations.literal: Originally avoiding the guilt of forbidden offense, dare return to the Minister of Crime;
translations.idiomatic: I fled a capital crime; I dare submit again to justice;

sentences.zh: 別族受封之典，誠愧諸侯。

translations.literal: Separate-surname receiving enfeoffment rites—truly ashamed before the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: yet to hold a fief under a false name shames me before the lords."

sentences.zh: 伏乞聖慈，許歸本姓」云云。

translations.literal: Kneeling beg sacred kindness, permit restoration of original surname," etc.
translations.idiomatic: I kneel and beg Your Majesty to let me bear my true name again," and so on.

sentences.zh: 其表甚為朝廷所重。

translations.literal: That memorial was greatly valued by the court.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that memorial in high regard.

sentences.zh: 後因汭生辰，淮南楊行密遣使致禮幣之外，仍貺《初學記》一部。

translations.literal: Later because of Rui's birthday Huainan Yang Xingmi sent envoys with ceremonial gifts besides, still bestowing one copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.
translations.idiomatic: On Rui's birthday Yang Xingmi sent gifts from Huainan—and added a copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.

sentences.zh: 準忿然以為不可，謂汭曰：「夫《初學記》，蓋訓童之書爾，今敵國交聘，以此書為貺，得非相輕之甚耶！

translations.literal: Zhun angrily deemed it unacceptable, told Rui: "The 《Elementary Studies》 is merely a book for instructing children; now enemy states exchange missions—using this book as a gift, is it not extreme mutual slight!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhun was furious and told Rui, "The 《Elementary Studies》 is a schoolbook for children. An enemy state sends it as a state gift—is that not open contempt?"

sentences.zh: 宜書責讓。

translations.literal: Should write to reprove and blame.
translations.idiomatic: You should answer with a written rebuke.

sentences.zh: 」汭不納，準自歎曰：「若然，見輕敵國，足彰幕府之無人也。

translations.literal: " Rui did not accept; Zhun sighed to himself: "If so, being slighted by the enemy state sufficiently shows the headquarters has no men.
translations.idiomatic: " Rui refused. Zhun sighed, "Accept this and we show the enemy our staff has no one with spine.

sentences.zh: 參佐無狀，安可久！

translations.literal: Staff officers unworthy—how can one long remain!
translations.idiomatic: I cannot serve such a court any longer!"

sentences.zh: 」遽請解職。

translations.literal: " Hastily requested dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: " He resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 汭怒其去，潛使人於途中殺之。）〉

translations.literal: Rui angry at his departure, secretly sent men on the road to kill him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Rui, enraged, had him murdered on the road home.)〉

sentences.zh: 杜洪者，江夏伶人。

translations.literal: Du Hong was a Jiangxia entertainer.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong had been an entertainer in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 鍾傳者，豫章小校。

translations.literal: Zhong Chuan was a Yuzhang junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chuan was a low officer in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟中，秦宗權凶焰飆起，屢擾江、淮，郡將不能城守。

translations.literal: In Tang Guangqi, Qin Zongquan's vicious flame rose like a whirlwind, repeatedly harassed Jiang and Huai; prefectural defenders could not hold the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi, Qin Zongquan ravaged the Jiang-Huai region until prefectural garrisons could no longer hold their walls.

sentences.zh: 洪、傳各為部校，因戰立威，逐其廉使，自稱留後，朝廷因而命之。

translations.literal: Hong and Chuan each were division officers; through battle established prestige, drove out their provincial inspectors, styled themselves acting governors; court thereby appointed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Chuan rose as unit commanders, fought their way to power, expelled their superiors, declared themselves acting governors, and won court recognition.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Du Hong and Zhong Chuan from the 《New Book of Tang》:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Du Hong and Zhong Chuan from the 《New Book of Tang》:

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》：光啟二年，洪乘虛入鄂，自為節度使留後，僖宗即拜本軍節度使。

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Guangqi year 2, Hong seized an opening to enter E, styled himself acting military commissioner, Emperor Xizong at once appointed him full army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says that in Guangqi 2 Hong seized Ezhou, made himself acting commissioner, and Xizong confirmed him.)

sentences.zh: 中和三年，傳逐江西觀察使高茂卿，遂有洪州，僖宗擢傳江西團練使，俄拜鎮南節度使。）〉

translations.literal: Zhonghe year 3, Chuan drove out Jiangxi observation commissioner Gao Maoqing, then held Hongzhou; Xizong promoted Chuan Jiangxi training commissioner, soon appointed Zhennan military commissioner.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (In Zhonghe 3 Chuan expelled Gao Maoqing from Jiangxi, took Hongzhou, and was made training commissioner, then Zhennan military commissioner.)〉

sentences.zh: 及為楊行密所攻，洪、傳首尾相應，皆遣求援於太祖；

translations.literal: When attacked by Yang Xingmi, Hong and Chuan head and tail responded, all sent seeking aid from the Founder;
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmi attacked them, Hong and Chuan backed each other and both appealed to the Founder;

sentences.zh: 太祖遣朱友恭赴之，大破淮寇於武昌，二鎮稍寧。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Zhu Yougong to go; greatly defeated Huainan bandits at Wuchang; the two prefectures gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Zhu Yougong, who routed the Huainan army at Wuchang and gave the two regions brief relief.

sentences.zh: 及行密乘勝急攻洪、鄂，洪復乞師於太祖；

translations.literal: When Xingmi seized victory to press attack on Hong and E, Hong again begged troops from the Founder;
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi pressed the attack on Hong and E, Hong again begged the Founder for troops;

sentences.zh: 太祖命荊南成汭率荊、襄舟師以赴之。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered Jingnan Cheng Rui to lead Jing and Xiang river fleets to go relieve.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder ordered Cheng Rui of Jingnan to sail the Jing-Xiang fleet to his aid.

sentences.zh: 未至夏口，汭敗溺死，淮人遂陷鄂州，洪為其所擒，被害於廣陵市，時唐天復二年也。

translations.literal: Before reaching Xiakou, Rui was defeated and drowned; Huainan men then took Ezhou; Hong was captured by them, killed at Guangling market—then Tang Tianfu year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Rui drowned in defeat before Xiakou; the Huainan army took Ezhou, seized Hong, and executed him at Guangling market in Tianfu 2.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Liu Cun from the 《Chronicle of the Nine States》:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Liu Cun from the 《Chronicle of the Nine States》:

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·劉存傳》：存急焚鄂州城樓，梁援兵將突圍而出，諸將欲急擊之，存曰：「擊之賊必復入，復入則城愈固矣，不若聽其遁去。

translations.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Liu Cun》: Cun urgently burned Ezhou's tower; Liang relief troops were about to break out; the generals wished to strike them hard; Cun said: "Strike them and the bandits will re-enter; re-enter and the city will be firmer still—better to let them escape.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says Liu Cun burned Ezhou's tower as Liang relief tried to break out. His officers wanted a hard strike; Cun said, "Hit them and they will rush back in and the wall will only tighten—let them go.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The generals all said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: " The generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 」是日城陷，擒杜洪父子，斬於廣陵市。）〉

translations.literal: " That day the city fell; Du Hong father and son were captured and beheaded at Guangling market.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " That day the city fell; Du Hong and his son were taken and beheaded at Guangling market.)〉

sentences.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖表請為洪立廟於其鎮，優詔可之。

translations.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder memorialized requesting a temple for Hong at his command; gracious edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder won approval for a temple to Du Hong in his old command.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，詔贈太傅。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founder took the throne, Hong was posthumously named Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 先是，鍾傳卒於江西，其子繼之，

translations.literal: Before this, Zhong Chuan died in Jiangxi; his son succeeded him,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhong Chuan had died in Jiangxi and his son succeeded him,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Qin Pei from the 《Chronicle of the Nine States》:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Qin Pei from the 《Chronicle of the Nine States》:

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·秦裴傳》：天祐三年，洪州鍾傳卒，州人立其子匡時。

translations.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Qin Pei》: Tianyou year 3, Hongzhou Zhong Chuan died; the prefecture's people installed his son Kuangshi.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that in Tianyou 3 Zhong Chuan died at Hongzhou and the people set up his son Kuangshi.)

sentences.zh: 江州刺史延規，傳之養子，忿不得立，以其郡納款，因授裴西南面行營招討使，攻匡時。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou prefect Yan Gui, Chuan's adoptive son, angry at not being installed, submitted his prefecture in surrender; therefore Pei was appointed southwest campaign pacification commissioner and attacked Kuangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gui, Chuan's adopted son and Jiangzhou prefect, resenting his exclusion, surrendered his prefecture; Qin Pei was sent to attack Kuangshi.

sentences.zh: 城陷，擒匡時以獻。）〉

translations.literal: The city fell; Kuangshi was captured and presented.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The city fell and Kuangshi was captured and sent in.)〉

sentences.zh: 尋為楊行密所敗，其地亦入於淮夷。

translations.literal: Soon defeated by Yang Xingmi; that territory too entered Huainan barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yang Xingmi defeated them and Jiangxi too passed to Huainan.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Zhong Chuan from the 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Zhong Chuan from the 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》:

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：鍾傳雖起於商販，尤好學重士，時江西上流有名第者，多因傳薦，四遠騰然，謂之曰英明。

translations.literal: (The 《Supplement》: Though Zhong Chuan rose from merchant peddlers, he especially loved learning and honored scholars; at that time famous clans of upper Jiangxi mostly entered through Chuan's recommendation; from the four quarters it soared—people called him "the enlightened one."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplement》 says Chuan began as a trader but prized learning and patronized scholars; eminent Jiangxi families often owed their posts to him, and men far and wide called him "the enlightened."

sentences.zh: 諸葛浩素有詞學，嘗為泗州管驛巡官，仰傳之風，因擇其所行事赫赫可稱者十條，列於啟事以投之。

translations.literal: Zhuge Hao always had literary learning; once was Sizhou postal-station patrol officer; admiring Chuan's reputation, he therefore selected ten items from Chuan's deeds that shone and could be praised, arrayed them in a memorial to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hao, a man of letters once posted at a Sizhou relay station, admired Chuan and sent a memorial listing ten of his finest deeds.

sentences.zh: 十啟凡五千字，皆文理典贍，傳覽之驚歎，謂賓佐曰：「此啟事每一字可以千錢酬之。

translations.literal: Ten memorials in all five thousand characters, all literary reasoning elegant and ample; Chuan on reading was startled and sighed, told his staff: "This memorial—each character can be rewarded with a thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: Ten sections, five thousand characters, all polished; Chuan read them in wonder and told his staff, "Every character in this is worth a thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 」遂以五千貫贈，仍辟在幕下，其激勸如此。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with five thousand strings he was gifted, still recruited to the headquarters—such was his encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave five thousand strings, took Hao onto his staff, and rewarded talent that lavishly.

sentences.zh: 上藍和尚，失其名，居於洪州上藍院，精究術數，大為鍾傳所禮。

translations.idiomatic: A monk of Shanglan Monastery in Hongzhou, name forgotten, was a master of divination whom Chuan treated with great respect.

translations.idiomatic: When the monk fell gravely ill Chuan visited him and said, "I have held nothing back from you—won't you leave me one word before you go?"

sentences.zh: 」上藍強起，索筆作偈以援，其末云：「但看來年二三月，柳條堪作打鍾槌。

translations.idiomatic: " The monk roused himself, wrote a verse, and ended it, "Watch the second or third month next year—willow twigs will do for beating the bell."

sentences.zh: 」偈終而卒。

translations.literal: Chuan obtained it and could not fathom it.

translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun had begun as a senior officer in the Yangzhou garrison.

translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanzhou's origins are unknown.

translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says he came from Shucheng in Luzhou.)〉

translations.literal: Early Tang Tianyou, Yang Xingmi heroically held Huai and Hai; then Yun was Xuancheng military commissioner, Yanzhou was Shou prefect magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianyou, Yang Xingmi dominated the Huai-Hai region; Yun held Xuancheng and Yanzhou held Shou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頵以行密專恣跋扈，嘗移書諷之曰：「侯王守方，以奉天子，古之制也。

translations.literal: Yun because Xingmi was willful and overbearing, once sent a letter admonishing him, saying: "Marquises and kings guard their regions to serve the Son of Heaven—this is the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yang Xingmi arrogant, Yun wrote to admonish him: "Princes are meant to guard their lands for the Son of Heaven—that is the ancient order.

sentences.zh: 其或逾越者，譬如百川不朝於海，雖狂奔猛注，澶漫遐廣，終為涸土，不若恬然順流，淼茫無窮也。

translations.literal: Whoever oversteps is like a hundred streams not paying court to the sea—though wildly rushing and pouring, vast and wide, in the end they become dry earth; better to calmly follow the current, boundless and without end.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever overreaches is like a stream that never reaches the sea: however fierce the flood, it ends in dust. Better to flow with the tide and never run dry."

sentences.zh: 況東南之鎮，楊為大，塵賤刀布，阜積金玉，願公上恒賦，頵將悉儲峙，具單車從。

translations.literal: Moreover among southeast commands Yang is greatest; dust and base coin and cloth, heaped gold and jade—may my lord remit the standing tax; Yun will store it all and follow with a single cart."
translations.idiomatic: "You are greatest in the southeast, piled with gold and goods. Send the regular tribute through me—I will store it and deliver it myself in one cart."

sentences.zh: 」行密怒曰：「今財賦之行，必由於汴，適足以資於敵也。

translations.literal: Xingmi angrily said: "Now the flow of wealth and levies must pass through Bian—just enough to enrich the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi snapped, "Revenue now must pass through Bian—that only feeds our enemy."

translations.idiomatic: " He refused.

translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was then holding Shouchun,

translations.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States》: Early Tianfu, the northern offices held the emperor on a western progress; Emperor Zhaozong hearing Yanzhou had martial talent sent Li Yan by hidden route bearing an edict appointing Yanzhou Cai prefecture military commissioner.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that early in Tianfu, with the court driven west, Zhaozong heard of Yanzhou's ability and sent Li Yan secretly to name him Cai commissioner.)〉

sentences.zh: 直頵之事，密遣人告於頵曰：「公有所欲為者，願為公執鞭。

translations.literal: Straight at Yun's affair, secretly sent men to tell Yun: "Whatever my lord wishes to do, I wish to hold the whip for my lord."
translations.idiomatic: With Yun's plot in mind, he secretly sent word: "Whatever you intend, I will serve as your man."

sentences.zh: 」頵聞之，頗會其志，乃召進士杜荀鶴具述其意，復語曰：「昌本朝，奉盟主，在斯一舉矣。

translations.literal: " Yun on hearing greatly grasped his intent, then summoned presented scholar Du Xunhe to fully relate his intent, again saying: "To prosper the dynasty, serve the alliance lord—it's in this one move."
translations.idiomatic: " Yun took his meaning, summoned the scholar Du Xunhe, laid out the plan, and said, "To restore the dynasty and serve our ally—everything hangs on this."

sentences.zh: 」即遣荀鶴具述密議，自間道至大梁。

translations.literal: " At once sent Xunhe to fully relate the secret design, by hidden route to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Xunhe by secret road to Daliang with the full plot.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，遽屯兵於宿州，以會其變。

translations.literal: The Founder greatly rejoiced and swiftly stationed troops at Suzhou to await their mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was delighted and rushed troops to Suzhou to meet the plot.

translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Xingmi's wife was Yanshou's sister and sent a persuader to call him.

translations.idiomatic: Warned by his sister's maid, Yanshou galloped to Yangzhou.)〉

translations.literal: Next he marshaled all troops to attack Xuancheng; Yun's defending strength was thin and few—he abandoned the walls and fled, could not cross the border, and was taken by Xingmi's army.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi then attacked Xuancheng; Yun, outmatched, fled the walls but was caught before he could escape the prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Tian Yun's defeat:

translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says Xingmi sent Tai Meng and Wang Maozhang by land while Yun fought at Guangde, was routed, and fled to Wanyang with survivors.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan and Wang Jian heard of the defeat and surrendered the whole fleet to Xingmi.

translations.idiomatic: Yanshou galloped toward Yangzhou; a stage short of the city, Xingmi's men killed him.

sentences.zh: 其後，延壽部曲有逸境至者，具言其事。

translations.literal: Afterward, of Yanshou's division there were those who escaped the border and came, fully narrating this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later fugitives from Yanshou's command told the full story.

sentences.zh: 又云：延壽之將行也，其室王氏勉延壽曰：「今若得兵柄，果成大志，是吉凶係乎時，非係於吾家也。

translations.literal: They also said: When Yanshou was about to depart, his wife the Wang clan urged Yanshou saying: "Now if you obtain military power and indeed achieve a great ambition, fortune and misfortune depend on the times, not on our household.
translations.idiomatic: They said that before he left, his wife Lady Wang urged him: "If you win command and your great ambition succeeds, fortune and ruin ride on the times, not on our house.

sentences.zh: 然願日致一介，以寧所懷。

translations.literal: Yet I wish each day to send one messenger, to quiet what the heart holds."
translations.idiomatic: Yet send me one messenger each day to ease my heart."

sentences.zh: 」一日，介不至，王氏曰：「事可知矣！

translations.idiomatic: When a day passed without word, Lady Wang said, "It is clear—

sentences.zh: 」乃部分家仆，悉授兵器，遽闔中扉，而捕騎已至，不得入。

translations.literal: " She then arrayed the household servants, all gave weapons, swiftly shut the inner doors—and the arresting horsemen had already arrived, could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: She armed the household, bolted the inner doors, and kept the arresting horsemen outside.

sentences.zh: 遂集家屬，阜私帑，發百燎，合州廨焚之。

translations.literal: Thereupon she gathered kin, heaped private treasuries, lit a hundred torches, and together with the prefectural offices burned them.
translations.idiomatic: She gathered her kin, piled the family treasury, lit a hundred fires, and burned the prefectural offices with them.

sentences.zh: 既而稽首上告曰：「妾誓不以皎然之軀，為仇者所辱。

translations.literal: Then she kowtowed upward and declared: "This wife vows not to let this pure body be shamed by enemies."
translations.idiomatic: Kowtowing, she declared, "I will not let my enemies dishonor this body."

sentences.zh: 」乃投火而死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she cast herself into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the flames and died.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Yang Xingmi's feigned blindness:

translations.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Yang Xingmi held Huainan; his wife's younger brother of the Zhu clan, whom the masses called Zhu the Third, Xingmi appointed defense commissioner of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says Xingmi made his brother-in-law Zhu, called Third Master Zhu, defense commissioner of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 泗州素屯軍，朱氏驍勇，到任恃眾自負，行密雖悔，度力未能製，但姑息之，時議以謂行密事勢去矣。

translations.literal: Sizhou always quartered troops; the Zhu clan was fierce and brave—on reaching office he relied on the masses and was self-important; Xingmi though regretted it, gauged his strength could not control him, only indulged him; at the time opinion held that Xingmi's situation and power were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou was garrison country; Zhu was fierce and swaggered in office while Xingmi, unable to curb him, only indulged him—observers thought Xingmi had lost his grip.

sentences.zh: 居無何，行密得目疾，雖愈，且詐稱失明，其出入皆以人扶策，不爾則觸牆抵柱，至於流血，姬妾仆隸以為實然，往往無禮，首尾僅三年。

translations.literal: After not long, Xingmi contracted eye disease; though cured, he yet falsely claimed blindness; going in and out he was always supported by men, otherwise he would strike walls and pillars, even to bleeding; concubines and servants thought it real and often were without propriety—for head and tail nearly three years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he suffered an eye ailment; though healed, he feigned blindness for nearly three years, needing guides and colliding with walls until servants and concubines took it for truth and grew insolent.

sentences.zh: 朱氏聞之，信而少懈馳，行密度其計必中，謂妻曰：「吾不幸臨老兩目如此，男女輩幼，苟不諱，則國家為他人所有。

translations.literal: The Zhu clan heard it, believed it, and slightly slackened vigilance; Xingmi gauged his plan would surely hit, and told his wife: "I am unlucky to face old age with both eyes thus; the boys and girls are young—if we do not take care, then the state will belong to others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu believed the blindness and relaxed his guard; Xingmi, sure his ruse had worked, told his wife: "I am old and blind, the children young—if we do not act, our realm will pass to another."

sentences.zh: 今晝夜思忖，不如召泗州三舅來，使管勾軍府事，則吾雖死無恨。

translations.literal: Now day and night I ponder—better to summon the third maternal uncle from Sizhou to manage military headquarters affairs; then though I die I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Better summon your third brother from Sizhou to run headquarters—then I can die content."

sentences.zh: 」妻以為然，遽發使述其意而召之。

translations.literal: The wife thought it right and swiftly sent envoys stating the intent and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: She agreed and sent envoys to summon him.

sentences.zh: 朱氏大喜，倍道而至。

translations.literal: The Zhu clan greatly rejoiced and came by double stages.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was overjoyed and came at forced march.

sentences.zh: 及入謁，行密恐其覺，坐於中堂，以家人禮見。

translations.literal: When he entered to pay respects, Xingmi feared he would detect it; he sat in the central hall and received him with family ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing discovery, Xingmi received him in the central hall with family rites.

sentences.zh: 朱氏頗有德色，方設拜，行密奮袖中鐵槌以擊之，正中其首，然猶宛轉號叫，久而方斃。

translations.literal: The Zhu clan had quite a virtuous countenance; just as he set to bow, Xingmi whipped out an iron mallet from his sleeve to strike him—square on the head; yet he still twisted and cried out, long before finally dead.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhu bowed, Xingmi struck him from his sleeve with an iron mallet; Zhu twisted and screamed a long while before he died.

sentences.zh: 行密內外不測，即時升堂廳，召將吏等謂之曰：「吾所以稱兩目失明者，蓋為朱三。

translations.literal: Inside and outside Xingmi's court could not fathom it; he at once ascended the hall chamber and summoned generals and clerks, telling them: "The reason I claimed both eyes blind was all for Zhu the Third.
translations.idiomatic: The court was stunned; Xingmi mounted the hall and told his officers: "I only pretended blindness for Zhu the Third.

sentences.zh: 此賊今擊殺，兩目無事矣，諸公知之否！

translations.literal: This villain is now struck dead; both eyes are unharmed—do you gentlemen know it or not!"
translations.idiomatic: That traitor is dead and my eyes are sound—do you understand?"

sentences.zh: 」於是軍府大駭，其仆妾嘗所無禮者皆自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon the military headquarters was greatly alarmed; the servants and concubines who had been without propriety all killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters panicked; servants and concubines who had been insolent killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 初，行密之在民間也，嘗為合肥縣手力，有過，縣令將鞭之，行密懼且拜。

translations.literal: At first, when Xingmi was among the people, he had been a Hefei county corvée laborer; he had an offense and the county magistrate was about to whip him—Xingmi feared and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as a corvée laborer in Hefei county, he faced a magistrate's whip and bowed in terror.

sentences.zh: 會有客自外入，見行密每拜，則廳之前簷皆叩地，而令不之覺。

translations.literal: A guest came in from outside and saw each time Xingmi bowed, then the hall's front eaves all struck the ground, while the magistrate did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: A visitor saw each bow shake the eaves to the ground while the magistrate noticed nothing.

sentences.zh: 客知其非常，乃遽升廳揖令於他處，告以所見，令驚，遂恕之，且勸事郡以自奮。

translations.literal: The guest knew he was extraordinary and swiftly ascended the hall to bow to the magistrate elsewhere, reporting what he had seen; the magistrate was alarmed, then pardoned him and also urged him to serve the commandery to exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: The guest knew him extraordinary, warned the magistrate, won a pardon, and urged him to serve the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 行密度本郡不足依，乃投高駢。

translations.literal: Xingmi gauged his native commandery insufficient to rely on and thereupon submitted to Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Hefei too small, he entered Gao Pian's service.

sentences.zh: 駢死，秦彥、孫儒等作亂，行密連誅之，遂有淮南之地。）〉

translations.idiomatic: After Pian's death he destroyed Qin Yan and Sun Ru and seized Huainan.)〉

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝，

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning,
translations.idiomatic: Next was Zhao Kuangning,

translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Zhao Kuangning's style name:

translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 gives his style as Guangyi.)〉

sentences.zh: 蔡州人也。

translations.literal: was a man of Cai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: was a native of Cai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父德諲，初事秦宗權為列校，當宗權強暴時，表為襄州留後。

translations.literal: Father Dexin at first served Qin Zongquan as a column commander; when Zongquan was violent and fierce, he memorialized him as Xiangzhou acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dexin served Qin Zongquan as a column commander and was made acting commissioner of Xiang when Zongquan grew violent.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟四年夏六月，德諲審宗權必敗，乃舉漢南之地以歸唐朝，仍遣使投分於太祖，兼誓戮力，同討宗權。

translations.literal: Tang Guangqi year 4 summer sixth month, Dexin judged Zongquan would surely be defeated and thereupon raised the Hannan lands to return to Tang, still sending envoys to declare separation to the Founder and jointly swearing united strength to attack Zongquan together.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, month 6 of Guangqi 4, Dexin saw Zongquan would fall, surrendered Hannan to Tang, sent envoys to the Founder, and swore to destroy Zongquan together.

sentences.zh: 時太祖為蔡州四面行營都統使，乃表德諲為副，仍領襄州節度使。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder was Caizhou four-sides campaign overall commander; he memorialized Dexin as deputy and still had him lead Xiangzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, then overall commander against Cai, made Dexin his deputy and confirmed him as Xiang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蔡州平，以功累加官爵，封淮安王。

translations.literal: When Cai prefecture was pacified, by merit offices and titles were repeatedly added; he was enfeoffed Prince of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai fell he rose in rank and was enfeoffed Prince of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 匡凝以父功為唐州刺史兼七州馬步軍都校。

translations.literal: Kuangning by his father's merit was Tang prefecture inspector and concurrent seven-prefecture horse-and-foot army overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning became Tang prefect inspector and overall commander of seven prefectures' horse and foot through his father's merit.

sentences.zh: 及德諲卒，匡凝自為襄州留後，朝廷即以旄鉞授之。

translations.literal: When Dexin died, Kuangning made himself Xiangzhou acting commissioner; the court thereupon bestowed the command baton and axe.
translations.idiomatic: When Dexin died Kuangning made himself acting commissioner and received the court commission.

sentences.zh: 作鎮數年，甚有威惠，累官至檢校太尉、兼中書令。

translations.literal: As commissioner for several years he had great authority and kindness; offices repeatedly reached Honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled Xiang for years with authority and kindness and rose to Honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 匡凝氣貌甚偉，好自修飾，每整衣冠，必使人持巨鑒前後照之。

translations.literal: Kuangning's bearing was very grand; he loved self-adornment—each time he arranged cap and robes he must have men hold great mirrors before and behind to shine on him.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and vain, he had great mirrors held before and behind him whenever he dressed.

sentences.zh: 對客之際，烏巾上微覺有塵，即令侍妓持紅拂以去之。

translations.literal: When facing guests, on the black cap he slightly sensed dust and at once ordered serving girls to hold red dusters to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: If he sensed dust on his black cap before guests, maids brushed it away with red dusters.

sentences.zh: 人有誤犯其家諱者，往往遭其木檟楚，其方嚴也如是。

translations.literal: Those who by mistake violated his family taboo often suffered his wooden cudgel beating—his severity was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who breached his name taboo risked a beating with a wooden club.

sentences.zh: 光化初，匡凝以太祖有清口之敗，密附於淮夷，太祖遣氏叔琮率師伐之。

translations.literal: At the start of Guanghua, Kuangning because the Founder had the Qingkou defeat secretly attached to the Huai barbarians; the Founder sent Clan Uncle Cong with troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guanghua, after the Founder's defeat at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly sided with the Huai rebels and the Founder sent Shi Shucong against him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其泌州刺史趙璠越墉來降，隨州刺史趙匡璘臨陣就擒。

translations.literal: Before long, his Bi prefecture inspector Zhao Fan scaled the wall to come surrender; Suizhou inspector Zhao Kuanglin at the battle line was captured on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his Bi inspector Zhao Fan climbed the wall to surrender and Suizhou inspector Zhao Kuanglin was taken in battle.

sentences.zh: 俄而康懷英攻下鄧州，匡凝懼，遣使乞盟，太祖許之，自是附庸於太祖。

translations.literal: Soon Kang Huaiying attacked and took Deng prefecture; Kuangning feared and sent envoys to beg alliance—the Founder permitted it; from then he was a vassal of the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Huaiying took Deng; Kuangning sued for peace, the Founder agreed, and he became a vassal.

sentences.zh: 及成汭敗於鄂州，匡凝表其弟匡明為荊南留後。

translations.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated at E prefecture, Kuangning memorialized his younger brother Kuangming as Jingnan acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng Rui fell at Ezhou, Kuangning had his brother Kuangming made acting Jingnan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時唐室微弱，諸道常賦多不上供，惟匡凝昆仲雖強據江山，然盡忠帝室，貢賦不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the Tang house was weak; many circuits' regular levies often did not go up in tribute—only Kuangning and his brothers, though strongly holding rivers and mountains, yet were wholly loyal to the imperial house and tribute and levies did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: While Tang weakened and most circuits withheld tribute, the Zhao brothers still sent loyal levies from their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 太祖將期受禪，以匡凝兄弟並據藩鎮，乃遣使先諭旨焉。

translations.literal: The Founder was about to fix the date to receive the abdication mandate; because Kuangning and his brothers both held frontier commissions, he sent envoys first to announce the intent.
translations.idiomatic: As the Founder prepared to take the throne, he sent envoys ahead to the Zhao brothers holding the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 匡凝對使者流涕，答以受國恩深，豈敢隨時妄有他誌。

translations.literal: Kuangning to the envoy wept and replied that the state's grace was deep—how dare he follow the times and rashly have another intent.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning wept before the envoy and said the state's grace was too deep for him to change sides with the times.

sentences.zh: 使者復命，太祖大怒。

translations.literal: The envoy returned to report; the Founder was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy returned; the Founder flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年秋七月，遣楊師厚率師討之。

translations.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn seventh month, he sent Yang Shihou to lead troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, month 7 of Tianyou 2, he sent Yang Shihou to attack him.

sentences.zh: 八月，太祖親領大軍南征，仍請削匡凝在身官爵。

translations.literal: Eighth month, the Founder personally led a great army south on campaign and still requested stripping Kuangning of his personal offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Month 8 the Founder marched south in person and had Kuangning stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 及師厚濟江，匡凝以兵數萬逆戰，大為師厚所敗，匡凝乃燔其舟，單舸急棹，沿漢而遁於金陵。

translations.literal: When Shihou crossed the river, Kuangning with tens of thousands of troops met him in battle and was greatly defeated by Shihou; Kuangning then burned his boats, in a single skiff urgently rowed, and along the Han fled to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou crossed the river; Kuangning met him with tens of thousands, was routed, burned his fleet, and fled alone up the Han to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 後卒於淮南。

translations.literal: Later he died in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in Huainan.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Kuangning's flight and death:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Kuangning's flight and death:

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》云：師厚由陰穀伐木為梁，匡凝以兵二萬瀕江戰，大敗，乃燔州，單舸夜奔揚州。

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Shihou by Yin Valley felled timber for beams; Kuangning with twenty thousand troops fought along the river, was greatly defeated, then burned the prefecture and in a single skiff fled by night to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Shihou bridged Yin Valley, Kuangning lost twenty thousand along the river, burned the prefecture, and fled by night to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密見之，曰：「君在鎮，輕車重馬輸於賊，今敗，乃歸我邪！

translations.literal: Xingmi saw him and said: "Lord, in your commission you sent light carts and heavy horses as tribute to the enemy—now defeated, you return to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi greeted him: "You fed the enemy from your post—now you come to me defeated?"

sentences.zh: 」匡明亦謀奔淮南，子承規諫曰：「昔諸葛兄弟分仕二國，若適揚州，是自取疑也。

translations.literal: Kuangming also planned to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui remonstrated: "In old times the Zhuge brothers each served a different state—if you go to Yangzhou, it is yourself inviting suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming meant to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui warned that like the Zhuge brothers serving rival states, going to Yangzhou would invite suspicion.

sentences.zh: 」匡明謂然，乃趨成都。

translations.literal: Kuangming thought it so and thereupon hastened to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming agreed and fled to Chengdu instead.

sentences.zh: 《歐陽史》云：行密厚遇匡凝，其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。

translations.literal: The 《History of Ouyang》 says: Xingmi treated Kuangning generously; afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo gradually was without courtesy to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang's 《History》 says Xingmi treated Kuangning well, but after Xingmi's death Yang Wo grew rude to him.

sentences.zh: 渥方宴食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。

translations.literal: Wo was just feasting and eating green plums; Kuangning looked at Wo and said: "Do not eat much—it brings children's fever."
translations.idiomatic: At a feast Wo ate green plums; Kuangning warned, "Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children."

sentences.zh: 」諸將以為慢，渥遣匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。）〉

translations.literal: The generals thought it disrespect; Wo sent Kuangning to Hailing and later Xu Wen killed him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Officers took it as insult; Wo exiled him to Hailing, where Xu Wen later killed him.)〉

sentences.zh: 初，匡凝好聚書，及敗，楊師厚獲數千卷於第，悉以來獻。

translations.literal: At first Kuangning loved gathering books; when defeated, Yang Shihou obtained several thousand scrolls at his residence and entirely brought them as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning had loved books; after his defeat Shihou seized thousands of scrolls from his house and presented them to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 匡凝弟匡明，字讚堯，幼以父貴，一子出身，為江陵府文學。

translations.literal: Kuangning's younger brother Kuangming, style name Zanyao, in youth by his father's eminence entered office as a single son—he was Jiangling prefecture literary officer.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Kuangming, styled Zanyao, entered office young as a literary officer at Jiangling through their father's rank.

sentences.zh: 及壯，以軍功曆繡、峽二州刺史。

translations.literal: When grown, by military merit he passed through Xiuxi and Xia prefecture inspector posts.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he won military merit as inspector of Xiuxi and Xia.

sentences.zh: 成汭之敗，其兄匡凝表為荊南留後。

translations.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated, his elder brother Kuangning memorialized him as Jingnan acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng Rui's defeat his brother made him acting Jingnan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未至鎮，而朗、陵之兵先據其城矣。

translations.literal: Before he reached the commission, Lang and Ling troops had already seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office, Lang and Ling forces had already seized the city.

sentences.zh: 匡明領兵逐之，遂鎮於渚宮。

translations.literal: Kuangming led troops to drive them off and then held commission at Zhugong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming drove them off and held court at Zhugong.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年秋，太祖既平襄州，遣楊師厚乘勝以趨荊門。

translations.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn, the Founder having pacified Xiangzhou sent Yang Shihou to ride the victory toward Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, Tianyou 2, after Xiang fell the Founder sent Shihou on toward Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 匡明懼，乃舉族上峽奔蜀，王建待以賓禮。

translations.literal: Kuangming feared and thereupon led his clan up the gorge to flee to Shu; Wang Jian received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming fled upriver to Shu with his clan; Wang Jian received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 及建稱帝，用為大理卿、工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Jian declared himself emperor, he used him as Grand Court of Review director and Works Ministry minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian became emperor he made him Grand Court director and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於蜀。

translations.literal: After long time he died in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shu many years later.

sentences.zh: 張佶，不知何郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, not knowing what commandery man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji—his native commandery is unknown.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Zhang Ji's origins:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Zhang Ji's origins:

sentences.zh: （《九國志》，佶，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》, Ji was a Chang'an man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says Ji was from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，以明經中第，累遷宣州從事，復為秦宗權行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the start of Qianning he passed the classics examination with honors, repeatedly rose to Xuancheng staff officer, again became Qin Zongquan campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qianning he passed the classics exam, served at Xuancheng, and became Qin Zongquan's campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 後與劉建峰據湖南，推建峰為帥。）〉

translations.literal: Later with Liu Jianfeng he seized Hunan and pushed Jianfeng as commander.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He later seized Hunan with Liu Jianfeng and made Jianfeng commander.)〉

sentences.zh: 唐乾寧初，劉建峰據湖南，獨邵州不賓，命都將馬殷討之，期歲未克，而建峰為部下所殺，軍亂，鄰寇且至。

translations.literal: At the start of Tang Qianning, Liu Jianfeng held Hunan; only Shaozhou would not submit; he ordered capital commander Ma Yin to attack it—a year passed without taking it, and Jianfeng was killed by subordinates, the army in disorder, neighboring enemies about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianning Liu Jianfeng held Hunan while Shaozhou held out; Ma Yin besieged it a year without success, then Jianfeng was murdered, the army mutinied, and enemies closed in.

sentences.zh: 是時，佶為行軍司馬，屬潭人謀帥，曰：「張行軍即所奉也。

translations.literal: At that time Ji was campaign marshal; Tan men plotted a commander, saying: "Campaign Commander Zhang is whom we uphold."
translations.idiomatic: Ji was campaign marshal; the Tan garrison chose him, saying, "We want Commander Zhang."

sentences.zh: 」佶不得已而視事，旬日之間，威聲大振，寇亦解去。

translations.literal: Ji had no way but to take office; within ten days authority and renown greatly shook, and the enemies also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ji took command unwillingly; within ten days his authority restored order and the enemies withdrew.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Zhang Ji yielding command:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Zhang Ji yielding command:

sentences.zh: （《九國志》，建峰將吏推佶為帥，佶將入府，常所乘馬忽爾踶齧不止，正中佶髀。

translations.literal: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》, Jianfeng's generals and clerks pushed Ji as commander; Ji was about to enter headquarters when the horse he always rode suddenly kicked and bit without stop, squarely striking Ji's thigh.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says as Ji entered headquarters his usual mount kicked and bit him square in the thigh.

sentences.zh: 佶謂將吏曰：「吾非汝主，當迎馬公為之。」）〉

translations.literal: Ji told the generals and clerks: "I am not your lord—you should welcome Lord Ma for it." )〉
translations.idiomatic: Ji told the officers, "I am not your lord—bring Lord Ma." )〉

sentences.zh: 乃謂將吏曰：「佶才能不如馬公，況朝廷重藩，非其人不可。

translations.literal: He then told the generals and clerks: "Ji's talent is not equal to Lord Ma's; moreover the court weighs frontier commissions—not a non-person can hold it."
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "I am no match for Ma Yin, and the court needs the right man for a frontier post."

sentences.zh: 」因以牘召，殷亦不疑，稟命而至。

translations.literal: Thereupon with a document he summoned him; Yin also did not doubt and received orders and came.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yin by document; Yin came without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 佶受拜謁，禮畢，命升階讓殷為帥。

translations.literal: Ji received his bow and courtesy; when ceremony finished he ordered ascending the steps and yielded Yin as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ji received his bow, then stepped aside and installed Yin as commander.

sentences.zh: 佶即趨下率眾抃賀。

translations.literal: Ji at once hurried down and led the masses in clapping congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ji hurried below and led the troops in acclaim.

sentences.zh: 乃自請率師代殷攻邵州，下之。

translations.literal: He then himself requested to lead troops in Yin's stead to attack Shaozhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops in Yin's place, took Shaozhou, and delivered it.

sentences.zh: 復為行軍司馬，垂二十年。

translations.literal: Again he was campaign marshal—for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as campaign marshal for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 殷果立勳，甚德佶。

translations.literal: Yin indeed established merit and deeply esteemed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yin prospered and held Ji in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 開平初，殷表佶為朗州永順軍節度使，累加檢校太傅、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the start of Kaiping, Yin memorialized Ji as Langzhou Yongshun army military commissioner; offices repeatedly added Honorary Grand Tutor and Fellow of the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiping Yin made him military commissioner of Langzhou's Yongshun army and Honorary Grand Tutor and Secretariat Fellow.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年夏四月，卒於位。

translations.literal: In Qianhua year 1, summer, fourth month, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhua 1, summer month 4, he died in office.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Ji's post:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Ji's post:

sentences.zh: （《九國志》：乾化初，移鎮桂林，卒於治所。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Histories of the Nine States》 says: At the beginning of Qianhua he was transferred to govern Guilin and died at his seat of government.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States》 says he moved to Guilin early in Qianhua and died at his headquarters.)〉

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Chamberlain Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Chamberlain Attendant.

sentences.zh: 雷滿，

translations.literal: Lei Man,
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Man's name:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Man's name:

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》：滿字秉仁。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Man's style name was Bingren.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Tang History》 gives his style as Bingren.)〉

sentences.zh: 武陵洞蠻也。

translations.literal: was a cave-barbarian of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: came from the Wuling cave tribes.

sentences.zh: 始為朗州小校，唐廣明初，王仙芝焚劫江陵。

translations.literal: At first he was a petty officer of Lang prefecture; at the beginning of Tang Guangming, Wang Xianzhi burned and plundered Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Langzhou corporal; when Wang Xianzhi sacked Jiangling in early Guangming,

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷以高駢為節度使，駢擢滿為裨將，以領蠻軍。

translations.literal: At that time the court appointed Gao Pian military commissioner; Pian promoted Man to deputy general to lead barbarian troops.
translations.idiomatic: the court sent Gao Pian as commissioner, and Pian made Man a deputy to lead tribal levies.

sentences.zh: 駢移鎮淮南，復隸部曲，以悍獷趫健知名。

translations.literal: When Pian shifted his garrison to Huainan, Man again belonged to his command; for fierce and unruly speed and strength he was famed.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian moved south, Man stayed in his retinue and won fame for ferocious speed.

sentences.zh: 中和初，擅率部兵自廣陵逃歸於朗，沿江恣殘暴，始為荊人大患矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe he on his own led his troops to flee from Guangling back to Lang, along the river wantonly cruel and violent, beginning to be a great affliction to the people of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Early Zhonghe he deserted Guangling for Langzhou and raided the Yangzi—Jing's nightmare had begun.

sentences.zh: 率一歲中三四移，兵入其郛，焚蕩驅掠而去。

translations.literal: Leading troops three or four times in a year he moved; when troops entered their outer walls they burned, swept, drove, and plundered and left.
translations.idiomatic: Three or four times a year his armies burned the suburbs and drove off the plunder.

sentences.zh: 唐朝姑務息兵，即以澧朗節度使授之。

translations.literal: The Tang court for the moment pursued resting arms and thereupon granted him the Li and Lang military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tang bought peace and gave him the Li-Lang commission.

sentences.zh: 累官至檢校太傅、同平章事。

translations.literal: By accumulation of office he reached honorary Grand Preceptor and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to honorary Grand Preceptor and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 滿貪穢慘毒，蓋非人類。

translations.literal: Man was greedy, foul, and cruelly poisonous—surely no human kind.
translations.idiomatic: Man's greed and cruelty were scarcely human.

sentences.zh: 又嘗於府署浚一深潭，構大亭於其上，每鄰道使車經由，必召宴於中，且言：「此水府也，中有蛟龍，奇怪萬態，惟餘能遊焉。

translations.literal: Again he once at the prefectural office dug a deep pool, built a great pavilion upon it; whenever neighboring circuit envoys' carriages passed through, he inevitably summoned them to feast within, and moreover said: "This is the water palace; within are flood-dragons, myriad strange forms—only I can roam it.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a deep pool at headquarters and built a pavilion over it; when envoys passed through he always feasted them there and boasted, "This is my water palace, full of dragons in ten thousand shapes—only I can swim it.

sentences.zh: 」或酒酣對客，即取筵中寶器亂擲於潭中，因自褫其衣，裸露其文身，遽躍入水底，遍取所擲寶器，戲弄於水面，久之方出，復整衣就坐，其詭誕如此。

translations.literal: " Sometimes when wine was deep facing guests, he at once took precious vessels from the feast and wildly threw them into the pool, then himself stripped his clothes, bared his tattooed body, abruptly leaped into the water bottom, everywhere took up the thrown precious vessels, sported with them on the water surface, long after only emerged, again straightened clothes and took seat—his freakish absurdity was thus.
translations.idiomatic: " When drunk he would hurl gold and jade from the table into the pool, strip to show his tattoos, dive after them, juggle them on the surface, then dress and sit down again—as grotesque as that.

sentences.zh: 及死，子彥恭繼之。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Yiangong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Yiangong took over.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Man's death and succession:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Man's death and succession:

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》：滿以天復元年卒，子彥威自立，弟彥恭結忠義節度使趙匡凝以逐彥威。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Man died in Tianfu year 1; son Yanwei established himself; younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Tang History》 says he died in Tianfu 1; Yanwei seized power until Yiangong, with Zhao Kuangning, ousted him.)〉

sentences.zh: 蠻蜒狡獪，深有父風，燼墟落，榜舟楫，上下於南郡、武昌之間，殆無人矣。

translations.literal: Barbarian serpents, crafty and cunning, deeply had the father's manner; burning ruins and villages, rowing boats and oars, up and down between Nanjun and Wuchang—nearly no people.
translations.idiomatic: Savage and sly like his father, he burned villages and raided by boat between Nanjun and Wuchang until hardly anyone remained.

sentences.zh: 又與淮、蜀結連，阻絕王命。

translations.literal: Again he linked with Huai and Shu, obstructing and cutting off the royal commands.
translations.idiomatic: He allied with Huai and Shu and blocked the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔湖南節度使馬殷、荊南節度使高季昌練精兵五千，遣將倪可福統之，下澧州，與潭兵合。

translations.literal: The Founder edicted Hunan military commissioner Ma Yin and Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jichang to drill elite troops five thousand, send general Ni Kefu to command them, descend on Li prefecture, and unite with Tan troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder ordered Ma Yin and Gao Jichang to send five thousand elite troops under Ni Kefu to take Li and join the Tan army.

sentences.zh: 先是，滿塹沅江，以周其壘，門臨長橋，勢不可入。

translations.literal: Earlier Man had moated the Yuan River to surround his ramparts; the gate faced a long bridge—momentum could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Man had moated the Yuan around his walls; the gate on the long bridge was impregnable.

sentences.zh: 殷極其兵力，攻圍周歲，彥恭食盡兵敗，間使求救於淮夷。

translations.literal: Yin exhausted his military strength; attack and siege a full year; Yiangong food exhausted, troops defeated, through envoys begged rescue from the Huai barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yin besieged a full year; starving and beaten, Yiangong sent to the Huai for aid.

sentences.zh: 及淮軍來援，高季昌逆戰於治津馬頭岸，大破之，俄而攻陷朗州，彥恭單棹遁去。

translations.literal: When Huai troops came to rescue, Gao Jichang met them in battle at Zhijin Matou Bank and greatly defeated them; soon he attacked and took Lang prefecture; Yiangong in a single punt fled away.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai reinforcements came, Gao Jichang routed them at Matou Bank, then took Langzhou as Yiangong fled alone in a skiff.

sentences.zh: 馬殷擒其弟彥雄及逆黨七人，械送至闕，皆斬於汴橋下，時開平二年十一月也。

translations.literal: Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yanxiong and seven rebel partisans, sent them in shackles to the capital—all were beheaded below Bian Bridge; it was Kaiping year 2, eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin seized Yanxiong and seven rebels, sent them to Bian—all were executed at Bian Bridge in Kaiping 2, month 11.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：成汭、鍾、杜、田、朱之流，皆因否運，雄據大藩，雖無濟代之勞，且有勤王之節，功雖不就，誌亦可嘉，若較其誠明，則田頵、延壽斯為優矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Cheng Rui, Zhong, Du, Tian, Zhu, and their kind all because of adverse fortune boldly held great circuits; although they had no merit of saving the age, yet they had the integrity of assisting the king; achievement although not accomplished, intention also may be praised—if comparing their sincerity and clarity, then Tian Yun and Yanshou are superior.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Cheng Rui, Zhong, Du, Tian, Zhu and the like seized great domains in dark times; they lacked power to save the realm yet showed loyalty to the throne; merit failed but intent deserves praise—of them Tian Yun and Yanshou showed the truest hearts.

sentences.zh: 匡凝一門昆仲，千里江山，失守藩垣，不克負荷，斯乃劉景升之子之徒歟！

translations.literal: Kuangning one family's brothers, a thousand li of rivers and mountains, lost guard of the frontier walls, could not bear the burden—is this not the sort of Liu Jingsheng's sons!
translations.idiomatic: The Kuangning brothers held a thousand li yet lost their domain and could not sustain it—were they not Liu Biao's sons reborn?

sentences.zh: 張佶有讓帥之賢，雷滿辱俾侯之寄，優劣可知矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji had the virtue of yielding command; Lei Man disgraced the entrustment of vice-lord—superior and inferior can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji showed the grace to yield command; Lei Man shamed the trust of a commissioner—the contrast tells all.
